title: Tech Note: Using Structure Resources for Initializing a Database

historical_commentary.text: This note explores using resources stored in the 4D structure file to initialize default records in new data files and embed serial number or other identifying information as a simple copy protection mechanism. The Mac-era resource fork approach is entirely obsolete — modern 4D uses different mechanisms for database initialization and does not rely on resource forks. However, the concept of seeding default data into new databases remains relevant.
related_updates: Resource fork-based storage is no longer used in modern 4D
Modern 4D uses the On Startup database method and other mechanisms for database initialization
License and copy protection are now handled through 4D's built-in license management system
